reason: The Book of Esther passage describes the persecution of the Jewish people by Haman's plot to destroy them throughout the Persian kingdom. When Mordecai and Esther learn of this threat, they do not accept blame for the suffering, nor do any leaders attribute the threat to the people's fault. Instead, Esther petitions King Ahasuerus to reverse the decree, presenting the Jews as victims of an unjust conspiracy. The narrative portrays the suffering as arising from external persecution and antisemitism, not from any failing or transgression by the Jewish people themselves. The subsequent Jewish defense against their enemies is presented as justified retaliation against those seeking their destruction. There is no depiction of leaders attributing the peril to the people's own guilt or shortcomings.
